Content: “Darius I of Persia [reigned `text(522)-text(486 B.C.E.)`] proceeded to establish twenty governments of the kind which the Persians call satrapies, assigning to each its governor, and fixing the tribute which was to be paid him by the several nations. And generally he joined together in one satrapy the nations that were neighbors. The following is an account of these governments, and of the yearly tribute which they paid to the king:
The Greeks and the Syrians paid a tribute of `text(seven hundred and sixty)` talents* of silver.
All Phoenicia, Palestine, and Cyprus to the borders of Egypt paid a tribute of `text(three hundred and fifty)` talents of silver.
From Egypt, and the neighboring parts of Libya, the tribute which came in was `text(seven hundred)` talents of silver.
From Babylonia, and the rest of Assyria, were drawn a `text(thousand)` talents of silver.
Such was the revenue which Darius derived from Asia and a small part of Libya.”
Copyright: Herodotus, Greek historian, The Histories, circa `text(430 B.C.E.)`
References: A talent was a measure of weight equal to approximately 60 pounds.
